title: measurement settings
content:
Hi folk, how can I change my measurement settings to show in cm in clo-set. my settings in user setting in unit system is set at cm, if I export a garment to clo-set , I get a prompt in clo-set that its set in inches, how do I get clo-set to be set in cm. Hoping that you guys can assist.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: You're very welcome! Hope you have a great day as well. :)
Reply 1: ❤️

Comment 2: Hi. On your Company Page, you have the Settings icon. In there, you can set the unit and the currency.
Reply 1: Hi good morning Lucile, many thanks and well noted, I will check it out today, hope you have a lovely day further. 🙂🙂👍🏻
content_description: Provide guidance on how to change measurement units to centimeters in Clo-Set to avoid export prompts showing inches.

title: 2026 Q1 Updates in CLO-SET: Streamlining Product Development Workflows
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202608/2a203b98da054e78a58c2719f03940d6/images/51b2e8c5532642ca9dfac8178bcdbb51whatsnew-4-q1.png)Q1 updates support fashion teams at both ends of product development: shaping concepts earlier and preparing production documentation with less manual work.

Explore what's new in [CLO-SET](https://style.clo-set.com/).

# [Moodboard & Concept Development]

Product development starts long before the first garment is created. During concept development, teams explore ideas, compare styling options, and set the creative direction.

**Compare more styling options with Multiple Mix & Match**

Finding the right collection direction usually means reviewing many outfit combinations. With the updated Multiple Mix & Match, teams can compare styling options in a single workspace and evaluate assortments before a concept moves into development.

![](https://support.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/54173355873689)

**Create more flexible mood boards**

The updated Pen Tool in Visual Board gives teams more freedom when building mood boards and concept presentations. Sketch ideas, highlight references, and mark up directions without leaving Visual Board.

![](https://support.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/54185241912217)

## [Design Development & Review]

New improvements to Quality Render and Annotation help teams review garments more accurately and deliver clearer feedback.

**Improve garment reviews with Quality Render**

The updated Quality Render improves transparency and layer visibility, so overlapping fabrics, trims, and construction details are easier to inspect during 3D garment reviews. A more accurate representation of each garment means teams catch issues earlier and decide with more confidence before the next revision.

![c0adb9dde7394ec79629ef6fa7569b2b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/2a203b98da054e78a58c2719f03940d6/images/c0adb9dde7394ec79629ef6fa7569b2bimage.png)

**Keep design feedback organized with Annotation**

Reviewers can now save viewpoints before creating annotations, so every comment points to the correct area of the garment. The improved marker workflow keeps multiple revision requests organized, and feedback stays traceable across review cycles.

![](https://support.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/56484104395929)

## [Production-Ready]

**Prepare digital tech packs in the Content Page**

Production preparation depends on technical information staying connected to each design. When a 3D garment created in CLO is uploaded to CLO-SET, the Content Page automatically generates key Tech Pack information, including BOM (Bill of Materials) and POM (Points of Measurement). Teams review and manage Tech Pack data alongside the 3D garment in one workspace instead of recreating technical documents by hand, which makes production preparation faster and more consistent.

![](https://support.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/56489051622169)
content_description: Discover how CLO-SET’s latest Q1 updates streamline fashion product development by enhancing concept creation, design review, and production-ready documentation.

title: How Fadinha 3D Studio Reduced Review Cycles by 67% with Connected Product Development
content:
![9f38955d31ff4074a8f494d4a5170cc7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/312ddfbc929947e7aee61d70a1ee9ef5/images/9f38955d31ff4074a8f494d4a5170cc74-10.png)

CLO-SET helps teams keep assets, versions, and feedback connected throughout product development.

In fashion product development, every style goes through multiple rounds of reviews, revisions, and approvals before reaching production. As styles, stakeholders, and review iterations multiply, teams need a single source of truth. Without connected product information, even small delays in locating the latest assets or understanding previous decisions can slow development, extend review cycles, and create unnecessary communication between teams.

Monica, Founder and Fashion Designer of Fadinha 3D Studio, ran into these challenges as her collections and client projects grew. Managing multiple styles meant coordinating renders, material references, client feedback, and design revisions across every stage of development. As more stakeholders joined, keeping everyone aligned with the latest product information became just as important as the design work itself.

![f4dcb3db9ff34832ad8a7080c5b2b7a4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/312ddfbc929947e7aee61d70a1ee9ef5/images/f4dcb3db9ff34832ad8a7080c5b2b7a42-10.png)

Digital assets, material references, render images, technical information, and review comments accumulate throughout development. The information itself is rarely lost. What happens instead is fragmentation: it spreads across cloud storage, messaging platforms, email threads, screenshots, and local folders. As review cycles progress, reconstructing context takes manual effort, whether that means finding the latest version, revisiting previous feedback, or confirming approved assets. Teams end up spending their time reconnecting scattered information before a meaningful review can even begin.

To address this, Monica adopted CLO-SET as a centralized workspace for product development. Assets, version history, annotations, and review feedback stayed connected within the same product instead of being distributed across multiple tools.

Rather than creating separate files for every revision, version history preserved each iteration in a continuous timeline, so comparing changes and understanding how a style evolved became simple. Materials and references lived in shared libraries, and annotations stayed attached directly to the 3D garment, which gave every stakeholder complete context during reviews.

![47aec2a4753a4a5a94646b5f92c7fa7a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/312ddfbc929947e7aee61d70a1ee9ef5/images/47aec2a4753a4a5a94646b5f92c7fa7a7-10.png)

The impact went beyond file organization. Monica's team no longer had to search for assets repeatedly, verify which revision was latest, or reconstruct previous discussions, and the review process became noticeably more efficient.

Review cycles were reduced by approximately 67%, and product decisions moved up to three times faster. Instead of long clarification rounds between clients and internal teams, everyone worked from the same product information through concept development, sample reviews, and final approvals. With fewer interruptions and better visibility into product history, reviews got more productive and approvals moved forward with confidence.

From concept review to final approval, every stakeholder could access the latest product information in one place. Reviews ran faster, and collaboration stayed clear across the whole development process.
content_description: CLO-SET streamlines fashion product development by centralizing assets, version history, and feedback to accelerate review cycles and improve team collaboration.
